Survodutide (BI 456906): GLP-1/Glucagon Dual Agonist — Research Dossier

Research compounds discussed for educational purposes. Not FDA-approved for human use where applicable. Consult a healthcare provider before use.

What Is Survodutide?

Survodutide (BI 456906) is an investigational once-weekly injectable peptide developed jointly by Boehringer Ingelheim and Zealand Pharma. It is a dual agonist that simultaneously activates both the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R) and the glucagon receptor (GCGR). Structurally, it is derived from oxyntomodulin — an endogenous post-meal hormone naturally secreted in the gut that activates both receptors — but engineered for a ~7-day half-life suitable for once-weekly dosing.

The rationale for targeting both receptors is additive: the GLP-1 component drives appetite suppression and glycemic control, while the glucagon receptor component activates hepatic fat oxidation and thermogenesis — mechanisms that pure GLP-1 agonists like semaglutide do not engage. This is the same general strategy as pemvidutide and mazdutide, but survodutide represents Boehringer Ingelheim and Zealand's iteration of the GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist class, with its own unique pharmacology.

Mechanism of Action

  • GLP-1 receptor agonism: Slows gastric emptying, suppresses appetite via hypothalamic GLP-1 pathways, and increases insulin secretion in a glucose-dependent manner.
  • Glucagon receptor agonism: Activates hepatic fat oxidation, increases energy expenditure (thermogenesis), and promotes mobilization of stored liver fat — the key mechanism explaining survodutide's strong MASLD (metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease) results.
  • Net glycemic effect: Glucagon receptor agonism can raise blood glucose, but this is counterbalanced by the GLP-1 component's insulin-stimulating and glucose-lowering effects. Net HbA1c reduction was observed in SYNCHRONIZE-2.

Key Research Findings

SYNCHRONIZE-1 — Obesity Without Type 2 Diabetes

  • Population: 725 adults with obesity (no T2D)
  • Duration: 76 weeks
  • Weight loss: Up to 16.6% (efficacy estimand) vs 3.2% placebo
  • Responders: 85.1% achieved ≥5% weight loss (vs 38.8% placebo)
  • Publication: The New England Journal of Medicine, simultaneous with ADA 2026 Scientific Sessions

SYNCHRONIZE-2 — Obesity With Type 2 Diabetes

  • Population: ~752 adults with obesity and T2D
  • Duration: 76 weeks
  • Weight loss: Up to 13.1% vs 3.1% placebo
  • HbA1c: Reduction up to 1.21% from baseline of 7.4%
  • Responders: 79.3% achieved ≥5% weight loss (vs 32.7% placebo)
  • Publication: The New England Journal of Medicine, October 1, 2026 (simultaneous EASD 2026)

SYNCHRONIZE-MASLD — Liver Fat Reduction

  • Statistically significant reduction in liver fat in adults with MASLD
  • Publication: Nature Medicine, 2026
  • Hepatic fat outcomes represent the strongest evidence for any GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist in MASLD alongside pemvidutide

SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT — Cardiovascular Outcomes

  • Cardiovascular outcomes trial; readout expected Q4 2026
  • Will assess major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in high-risk populations

Dosing in Research

In the SYNCHRONIZE Phase 3 trials, survodutide was administered as subcutaneous once-weekly injections at doses of 3.6 mg and 6.0 mg (the two highest efficacy doses). An escalation schedule is used in clinical protocols. Exact dosing for any potential clinical use would be determined by regulatory approval — no dose has been approved for prescription.

Frequently Asked Questions

How does survodutide compare to semaglutide and tirzepatide for weight loss?

Survodutide's Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-1 (no T2D) reported 16.6% mean body weight loss — comparable to tirzepatide (~20-22% at highest doses) and better than semaglutide (~15%). In type 2 diabetes (SYNCHRONIZE-2), weight loss was 13.1%, published in NEJM October 2026, alongside an HbA1c reduction of 1.21%. Survodutide's glucagon receptor component gives it best-in-class liver fat reduction vs pure GLP-1 agents. No regulatory filing has been announced as of October 2026.

What is the mechanism of survodutide and why does the glucagon component matter?

Survodutide is derived from oxyntomodulin, an endogenous post-meal hormone activating both GLP-1R and GCGR. The GLP-1 arm suppresses appetite and slows gastric emptying; the glucagon receptor arm drives hepatic fat oxidation and thermogenesis. This dual mechanism explains survodutide's strong MASLD results (Nature Medicine 2026) — mechanisms pure GLP-1 drugs like semaglutide do not engage.

Is survodutide approved or available anywhere?

No. As of October 2026, survodutide is not approved in any country. Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-1, SYNCHRONIZE-2, and SYNCHRONIZE-MASLD are complete with positive results. SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT is pending. No regulatory filing has been publicly announced. Research-peptide vendors sell it unlicensed with no quality control — not recommended outside of approved clinical trial protocols.

Research Limitations

  • No regulatory approval — Phase 3 complete but no NDA/MAA filed as of October 2026
  • GI adverse events (nausea, vomiting) led to ~26% discontinuation in SYNCHRONIZE-2, vs 9% on placebo — higher than seen with some GLP-1 mono-agonists
  • Cardiovascular safety data (SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT) still pending
  • Comparison to other GLP-1/glucagon dual agonists (pemvidutide, mazdutide) in head-to-head trials not yet available
  • Long-term weight maintenance post-treatment data not yet established
